items.title: Buffett calls derivatives a 'time bomb'
items.summary: Warren Buffett's annual letter called derivatives (financial contracts whose value depends on something else) 'financial weapons of mass destruction' and warned of a mega-catastrophic risk.
items.label: Buffett warns on derivatives

items.title: Fed cuts its rate to 1 percent
items.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee lowered its target for the federal funds rate (the rate banks charge each other overnight) by a quarter of a percentage point to 1 percent.

items.title: Greenspan suggests more mortgage choices
items.summary: Alan Greenspan said American homeowners might benefit if lenders offered more alternatives to the traditional fixed-rate mortgage.

items.title: Fed raises its rate to 1.25 percent
items.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee raised its target for the federal funds rate by a quarter of a percentage point to 1-1/4 percent.

items.title: Fed raises its rate to 3.25 percent
items.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee raised its target for the federal funds rate by a quarter point to 3-1/4 percent.

items.title: Rajan warns of a small chance of meltdown
items.summary: At Jackson Hole, IMF chief economist Raghuram Rajan said incentives had raised the chance, still small, of a catastrophic meltdown.
items.label: Rajan warns at Jackson Hole

items.title: Shiller questions the housing boom
items.summary: Robert Shiller's 2005 second edition of Irrational Exuberance said the housing boom looked like the 1990s stock bubble and prices might fall for years.
items.label: Shiller warns on housing

items.title: Fed lifts its rate to 5.25 percent
items.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee raised its target for the federal funds rate by a quarter point to 5-1/4 percent.

items.title: US house prices reach their peak
items.summary: The S&P Case-Shiller 20-city index reached its all-time high of 206.52 in July 2006, after which US house prices fell.
items.label: House prices peak

items.title: US homeownership rate reaches 69 percent
items.summary: In 2006, 69 percent of US households owned their homes, up from 65 percent in 1995, Ben Bernanke said in a 2007 speech.

items.title: HSBC warns of $10.5bn of bad debts
items.summary: HSBC said its bad debt provisions for 2006 would be about $10.5bn, 20 percent more than expected, after US mortgage defaults rose.
items.label: HSBC bad debt warning

items.title: New Century shares are suspended
items.summary: Trading in New Century Financial, one of the largest US subprime lenders (subprime means lending to people with a poor credit history), was suspended amid fears that it might go bankrupt.

items.title: Bernanke says subprime impact may be contained
items.summary: In testimony, Fed chairman Ben Bernanke said the impact of subprime problems on the wider economy and markets seemed likely to be contained.
items.label: Bernanke: 'contained'

items.title: Subprime lender New Century files for bankruptcy
items.summary: New Century Financial filed for Chapter 11 protection and said it would cut 3,200 jobs, more than half its workforce.

items.title: Bernanke sets out the subprime worries
items.summary: At a Chicago Fed conference, Bernanke said rising subprime delinquencies and foreclosures raised important economic and social issues.
items.label: Bernanke on subprime

items.title: Merrill Lynch seizes Bear Stearns fund assets
items.summary: Merrill Lynch seized and sold $800m of bonds that were being used as collateral for loans to two Bear Stearns hedge funds.

items.title: Bear Stearns lends $3.2bn to a mortgage fund
items.summary: Bear Stearns said it would lend $3.2bn to one of its hedge funds after its bets on subprime debt went wrong.

items.title: Citigroup's Prince: 'We're still dancing'
items.summary: Citigroup chief executive Chuck Prince said that while the music was playing, the bank had to keep getting up to dance.
items.label: Prince: 'still dancing'

items.title: Bear Stearns tells fund investors they lost money
items.summary: Bear Stearns said investors in two hedge funds it had rescued would get little, if any, of their money back.

items.title: Bear Stearns halts withdrawals from third fund
items.summary: Bear Stearns stopped clients withdrawing cash from a third fund and filed for bankruptcy protection for the two it had rescued.

items.title: American Home Mortgage files for bankruptcy
items.summary: American Home Mortgage, one of the largest independent US home lenders, filed for bankruptcy after laying off most of its staff.

items.title: BNP Paribas freezes three funds
items.summary: BNP Paribas suspended three funds worth 2bn euros because it could not value their assets after liquidity 'evaporated'.
items.label: Credit markets freeze

items.title: Northern Rock asks the Bank of England for help
items.summary: The BBC reported that Northern Rock had been granted emergency support from the Bank of England as its funding dried up.

items.title: Savers queue to withdraw from Northern Rock
items.summary: Depositors withdrew about GBP 1bn a day after news of the Bank of England loan, the biggest run on a British bank in over a century.
items.label: Run on Northern Rock

items.title: Fed cuts its rate to 4.75 percent
items.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee lowered its target for the federal funds rate by half a percentage point to 4-3/4 percent.

items.title: UBS writes down $3.4bn on subprime debt
items.summary: UBS became the first top-flight bank to announce losses from subprime investments (a write-down: a cut in the value it puts on assets), and its chairman and chief executive stepped down.

items.title: Dow closes at a record 14,164.53
items.summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at its all-time high of 14,164.53 on 9 October 2007.
items.label: Dow peak

items.title: Big banks plan a $100bn fund for shaky debt
items.summary: Citigroup, JPMorgan Chase and Bank of America said they would guarantee credit to move loss-making mortgage assets off other firms' books.

items.title: Merrill Lynch chief Stan O'Neal leaves
items.summary: Stan O'Neal left Merrill Lynch after the bank disclosed $7.9bn of losses on mortgage-related investments.

items.title: Fed cuts its rate to 4.5 percent
items.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee lowered its target for the federal funds rate by a quarter of a percentage point to 4-1/2 percent.

items.title: Analyst warns Citigroup may need $30bn
items.summary: Late on 31 October 2007 Meredith Whitney of CIBC cut her rating on Citigroup and said a $30bn capital shortfall might force a dividend cut.
items.label: Whitney warns on Citi

items.title: Citigroup chief Charles Prince resigns
items.summary: Charles Prince stepped down after Citigroup said it would write off between $8bn and $11bn on subprime-related holdings.

items.title: Abu Dhabi buys a $7.5bn stake in Citigroup
items.summary: Citigroup sold a 4.9 percent stake to the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority for $7.5bn to strengthen its capital.

items.title: RBS loses GBP 19bn of market value in 2007
items.summary: The Guardian reported that GBP 19bn had been wiped off RBS's market value (what all its shares are worth) that year, with GBP 950m written off US subprime holdings.

items.title: Five central banks act together on funding
items.summary: The Fed, the ECB, the Bank of England and others offered billions of dollars in loans to banks to ease year-end funding pressure.

items.title: S&P downgrades bond insurers' ratings
items.summary: Standard & Poor's cut its investment ratings on several monoline insurers that guaranteed bond repayments.

items.title: Bank of America to buy Countrywide
items.summary: Bank of America agreed to buy Countrywide Financial, the largest US mortgage lender, for about $4bn in stock.

items.title: Fed cuts three quarters of a percentage point in an emergency
items.summary: The FOMC (the Fed's rate-setting committee) cut its target for the federal funds rate by three quarters of a point to 3-1/2 percent, its biggest cut in 25 years.

items.title: Bond insurer MBIA reports a $2.3bn loss
items.summary: MBIA, which insured bonds against default, reported a $2.3bn quarterly loss on its exposure to subprime mortgages.

items.title: Northern Rock is taken into public ownership
items.summary: After rejecting private rescue bids, the UK government nationalised Northern Rock.

items.title: JPMorgan rescues Bear Stearns for $2 a share
items.summary: With $30bn of central bank support, JPMorgan agreed to buy Bear Stearns, whose shares had collapsed the week before.
items.label: Bear Stearns rescue

items.title: Regulators seize IndyMac Bank
items.summary: IndyMac Bank, with $32bn of assets, failed and was reopened as IndyMac Federal Bank.

items.title: Treasury moves to support Fannie and Freddie
items.summary: The Treasury and the Fed announced steps to shore up Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, including credit access and possible share purchases.

items.title: US takes control of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac
items.summary: The regulator put the two mortgage finance companies into conservatorship, with Treasury support for their debts.
items.label: Fannie and Freddie seized

items.title: Bank of America buys Merrill Lynch for $50bn
items.summary: Bank of America agreed to buy Merrill Lynch for about $50bn in stock, or $29 a share, as Lehman collapsed.

items.title: Lehman Brothers files for bankruptcy
items.summary: Lehman Brothers filed for Chapter 11 protection after the US government refused to bail it out.
items.label: Lehman fails

items.title: Fed lends AIG up to $85bn
items.summary: The Federal Reserve Board authorised the New York Fed to lend AIG up to $85bn in return for an 80 percent stake.
items.label: AIG rescued

items.title: A money market fund breaks the buck
items.summary: A large money market fund said it could not repay shares at $1 after losses on Lehman debt, and investors pulled money out.
items.label: Money funds break

items.title: Lloyds TSB agrees to buy HBOS for GBP 12bn
items.summary: Lloyds TSB agreed to take over HBOS, Britain's largest mortgage lender, after a run on HBOS shares.

items.title: Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley become banks
items.summary: The Fed approved their applications to become bank holding companies, ending the stand-alone investment bank model.
items.label: Goldman, Morgan become banks

items.title: Berkshire puts $5bn into Goldman Sachs
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway bought $5bn of Goldman Sachs preferred stock and the right to buy $5bn more in shares.

items.title: FDIC seizes Washington Mutual
items.summary: Regulators closed Washington Mutual, with $307bn of assets, and sold its banking operations to JPMorgan Chase for $1.9bn.

items.title: House rejects the $700bn bank rescue
items.summary: The House of Representatives voted down the rescue bill, and the Dow fell 770 points, its biggest one-day points fall.

items.title: Congress passes the $700bn bank rescue
items.summary: The House approved the $700bn rescue plan by 263 votes to 171, four days after rejecting an earlier version.
items.label: Bank rescue becomes law

items.title: Wells Fargo agrees to buy Wachovia
items.summary: Wells Fargo offered about $15.1bn in stock for Wachovia, beating Citigroup's government-backed bid.

items.title: Central banks cut rates together
items.summary: The Fed, the ECB, the Bank of England and others cut rates by half a point; the Fed's target fell to 1-1/2 percent.

items.title: UK puts GBP 37bn into RBS, Lloyds and HBOS
items.summary: The UK government announced a GBP 37bn recapitalisation of Royal Bank of Scotland, Lloyds TSB and HBOS.

items.title: Switzerland rescues UBS
items.summary: The Swiss government put $60bn into UBS, moved $50bn of its troubled assets to a state fund and took a 9.3 percent stake.

items.title: Citigroup's market value falls to $25bn
items.summary: Citigroup shares fell more than 26 percent in a day, leaving the bank with a market value of about $25bn.

items.title: US backs $306bn of Citigroup assets
items.summary: The Treasury, the Fed and the FDIC agreed to cover losses on about $306bn of Citigroup assets and inject $20bn more capital.

items.title: Fed opens a $200bn lending scheme
items.summary: The Fed created the Term Asset-Backed Securities Loan Facility to lend against securities backed by consumer and small business loans.

items.title: Fed cuts its rate to near zero
items.summary: The FOMC set a target range of 0 to 1/4 percent for the federal funds rate, the lowest since records began.

items.title: Citigroup splits in two after an $8.29bn loss
items.summary: Citigroup reported an $8.29bn quarterly loss and said it would separate its traditional bank from its riskier businesses.

items.title: Obama signs a $787bn stimulus plan
items.summary: President Obama signed the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act, a $787bn package of spending and tax cuts.

items.title: AIG reports a $61.7bn quarterly loss
items.summary: AIG posted the largest quarterly loss in US corporate history and won another $30bn from the government.

items.title: Dow falls to a 12-year low
items.summary: The Dow closed at 6,547.05, its lowest since April 1997 and about 54 percent below its October 2007 record.
items.label: Market bottom

items.title: Citigroup shares jump on profit news
items.summary: Citigroup shares rose about 25 percent after chief executive Vikram Pandit said the bank was profitable in January and February.

items.title: Fed to buy $300bn of Treasury debt
items.summary: The FOMC said it would buy up to $300bn of longer-term Treasury securities and more mortgage-backed debt (home loans bundled together and sold as bonds).

items.title: Fed publishes bank stress test results
items.summary: The Fed, the OCC and the FDIC released the results of capital tests on the 19 largest US banks.

items.title: The US recession ends after 18 months
items.summary: The recession that began in December 2007 ended in June 2009, the longest downturn since World War II.
